spec.astemes_lib_lunit-1.11.2.6.spec: [Package] Name="astemes_lib_lunit" Version="1.11.2.6" Release="" ID=b2ad17a13868d42b2296ea226603d054 File Format="vip" Format Version="2017" Display Name="LUnit" [Description] Description="LUnit is a LabVIEW Unit Testing Framework built on the xUnit unit testing model and inspired by JKI VI Tester. LUnit helps you test driving your LabVIEW development and provides the following key features.\0A\0A- Fast test execution\0A- Clear and informative results view\0A- Run specific tests quickly from right-click menu\0A- Test results visible directly in LabVIEW project explorer\0A- Instant loading of UI\0A- Parallel test execution managed by framework\0A- LabVIEW API\0A- Support for extenssion through add-ons\0A\0ALUnit is integrated into the LabVIEW development environment and the functionality is accessed through the Tools->LUnit menu. From the menu, you may create a new tests or open the LUnit UI to run tests. Tests may also be executed directly from the project explorer by right-clicking on a Test Case and selecting Run Test Case... from the menu.\0A\0AFrom Quick Drop window (ctrl+space) use:\0A - Ctrl+L to run all tests within active project\0A - Ctrl+Shift+L to run all test cases with tests calling into the current VI\0A\0AThere are a few examples installed with LUnit and these may be found through the NI Example Finder using the keyword LUnit. The examples are installed at C:\\Program Files (x86)\\National Instruments\\LabVIEW 20XX\\examples\\Astemes\\LUnit by default.\0A\0ADocumentation is available on https://lunit.astemes.com." Summary="Unit testing framework for LabVIEW" License="MIT" Copyright="Copyright (c) 2020, Astemes" Distribution="" Vendor="Astemes" URL="https://lunit.astemes.com" Packager="Anton Sundqvist" Demo="FALSE" Release Notes="Fix issue #27 - Improved results window for parameterized test addon. Clicking a parameter opens the Parameters.vi\0AFix issue #30 - Improved details to JUnit xml report format. This resolves issues with more strict JUnit xml report parsers, such as the Dorny Test Reporter.\0AFix issue #31 - API now accepts a directory containing tests as input. This means that you do not need to organize tests in a LabVIEW project and can have LUnit run e.g. all tests in a /tests directory. This works directly with existing CLI tools such as LUnit CLI or LUnit for GCLI without any additional updates."
